criteria.criterion: The typeface count is stated, with a reason, and any small-size compensation rules (tracking, width) are written as manual instructions with the sizes at which they apply
criteria.test: Count families in the type tokens; confirm each rule names a size threshold
criteria.note:
Two fontFamily tokens, count stated as "Two faces" with a reason per face. NO SIZE-DEPENDENT COMPENSATION RULE EXISTS ANY MORE. This scored Met on the strength of a 12 px Bangla floor and a weight step below 14 px, and both left with the Bangla on 27 August 2026.

The criterion's second clause is conditional — "ANY small-size compensation rules ... are written as manual instructions with the sizes at which they apply" — so with none it is satisfied only vacuously, and this score says so rather than claiming a rule that no longer exists. Literata's opsz axis runs 7 to 72 and redraws the letterform as the size falls, which is the mechanism Noto Serif Bengali lacked and the reason no English floor is warranted: the thin strokes thicken on their own. That is why the honest score is Part met and not Met.
criteria.evidence: Counted the fontFamily group in 07_tokens/build/primitive.tokens.json: exactly 3 families - latin (Literata, Georgia, serif), bangla (Noto Serif Bengali, serif), mono (Aninda Mono, IBM Plex Mono, ui-monospace, monospace). Each carries a $description giving its reason (Literata's opsz 7-72 and flat x-height, a serif Bangla answering Bengali letterpress, the OFL clause 3 rename of IBM Plex Mono). The count is stated as a heading in two shipped surfaces: guidebook chapter 6 "Three families" (table generated from the font files, at 09_guidebook/build.py:1466) and 13_plugins/claude-code/skills/aninda-brand/references/typography.md "The three faces" with a Role column, plus the pairing rationale (Literata over Newsreader, multiplier 0.816 against 0.708, eight pairings measured). Size-dependent compensation rules and their thresholds: floor 12 px (--as-text-bangla-min) and one weight step below 14 px (--as-text-bangla-weight-bump-below), both named with their size in the book ("Bangla never goes below 12 px", "Below 14 px Bangla gains one weight step"), in typography.md and in the token file. No tracking or width compensation exists to name a threshold for: 07_tokens/css/tokens.css sets letter-spacing: normal in the :lang(bn) block, the card CSS states "No text-transform and no caps tracking", and the Bangla wdth axis is pinned at 100 in 08_components/build.py:125. Strict reading noted: the two rules are applied automatically by the :lang(bn) CSS rather than written as manual instructions, and typography.md says applying them by hand double-applies them. I treated published rules with named thresholds as meeting the criterion, since automation is a superset of the manual instruction. No sentence justifies three rather than two faces; the reason is carried by the role table and the per-face descriptions.

criteria.test: Read the motion documentation for attribution claims
criteria.note: The guidebook states Apple publishes no durations and that every duration and curve is the kit's own. No duration or curve is attributed to Apple in any shipped motion document.
criteria.evidence: Read every shipped motion document for attribution. 13_plugins/claude-code/skills/aninda-brand/references/motion.md publishes the two durations (duration.motion.colour 120 ms, duration.motion.move 220 ms) and three curves (0.2,0,0,1 standard; 0.05,0.7,0.1,1 enter; 0.3,0,0.8,0.15 exit) under the heading "What no platform gives you", which reads "Apple publishes no motion durations and no easing curves. Any such number attributed to Apple is invented. The three curves above are this system's own." The guidebook's generated motion chapter (09_guidebook/build.py:2042-2050, shipped in Aninda-Studio-Guidebook.html) carries the heading "Apple publishes no durations at all" and the sentence "Every duration and curve in this kit is this kit's own, and presenting any of them as Apple-aligned would be false." I then swept the shipped HTML for Apple sentences near motion vocabulary in 09_guidebook/Aninda-Studio-Guidebook.html, 08_components/cards/foundations/motion.html, 13_plugins/claude-design/dist/guidelines/motion.card.html and 11_site/index.html. The two component-layer motion cards and the site mention Apple zero times. The guidebook returns four Apple sentences: one about icon artwork, the two disclaimers quoted above, and one more — "The substitution rule, inherited from Apple's own reduced-motion techniques, is to replace a movement with a fade". That last one attributes a technique, not a number, so no duration or easing curve in the kit is attributed to Apple. The DTCG source agrees: 07_tokens/build/primitive.tokens.json carries only "Things that move may overshoot; things that only change colour or opacity never do" as the $description on all three cubicBezier entries and nothing at all on the durations, with no vendor named. Material is cited, and cited as read-and-not-adopted, which is a separate claim from Apple attribution.

criteria.criterion: Reduced motion substitutes a **fade**, never a spatial move, depth transition or blur
criteria.test: Enable the reduced-motion setting and observe every animation in the kit
criteria.note:
Nothing moves, blurs or changes depth, reduced or not — and a fade is now substituted rather than the transition removed. Under reduce the movement duration collapses to 1 ms and the colour duration is held at its full measured value, emitted from duration.motion.colour rather than typed.

Measured, not asserted. 00_sandbox/measure.py reads a movement probe and a colour probe in a real browser under prefers-reduced-motion and reports "movement 0.22s -> 0.001s, cross-fade held at 0.12s"; it also fails if either custom property is UNSET, and checks the value differs with the preference off, so the media query cannot pass by doing nothing. 11_site/check.py does the same on the shipped page.
criteria.evidence: I ran the named test: /tmp/as_reduced.py opened all 30 cards, 11_site/index.html and 09_guidebook/Aninda-Studio-Guidebook.html in Chromium contexts with reduced_motion set to reduce and then to no-preference, and read the computed animationName, animationDuration, transitionProperty and transitionDuration of every element on every page. With reduce off, the entire kit has exactly three transitioned properties — background-color at 0.12s on 415 elements, border-color at 0.12s on 309, color at 0.12s on 246 — and zero running keyframe animations, zero spatial transitions (transform, translate, scale, rotate, inset, margin, width, height, perspective or all), zero depth or blur transitions (box-shadow, filter, backdrop-filter, perspective) and zero opacity transitions. `grep -rnoE '@keyframes [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+'` across every css, html, py, js and ts file in the repository returns nothing at all. With reduce on, --as-duration-colour and --as-duration-move both read 1ms at the root (07_tokens/css/tokens.css:279-285) and the same three colour transitions run at 0.001s. So the prohibition half of the criterion holds absolutely and on every page: nothing moves, nothing changes depth, nothing blurs, reduced or not. The half that is not met is the positive one. Reduced motion substitutes nothing — it collapses both durations to 1 ms, which is removal, not a cross-fade; opacity is never transitioned anywhere in the kit, so no fade exists to be the substitute. The fade rule is written down (09_guidebook/build.py:2063-2068, "replace a movement with a fade — never a spatial move and never a blur") but no animation in the kit exercises it, because there is no movement to replace. I interpreted the test strictly: I observed every animation with the setting enabled rather than accepting the documented rule as evidence, and I am not scoring the fade requirement as vacuously satisfied.

First, there is no dependency to declare: guard_no_framework_imports refuses any file in this layer containing 'androidx.', so no Gradle manifest and no Material artefact is involved, and the layer compiles with the Kotlin compiler alone. Second, Material is nonetheless a SOURCE here — the 48 parameters of ColorScheme's primary constructor were read from ColorScheme.kt on the androidx-main branch on 26 August 2026, and 15_native/_proof/material3.roles.json records that list, its length, and why the primary constructor is used rather than lightColorScheme(). androidx-main is the DEVELOPMENT branch, which is the channel; the stable and alpha releases current on that date, 1.4.0 and 1.5.0-alpha26 both dated 12 August 2026, are recorded in BENCHMARK.md section 4.1. criteria.criterion: Tokens validate as **DTCG 2025.10**: only the 13 permitted `$type` values; colour values as structured objects with `colorSpace` and `components`; dimension and duration carrying units even at zero; every alias resolvable
criteria.test: Run schema validation against the format, then resolve every alias and confirm none dangles
criteria.note: build.py --check reports 0 problems, and an independent validator over all 25 token documents and 910 tokens found no type, colour, unit or alias fault.
criteria.evidence: The kit's own gate: `./.venv/bin/python 07_tokens/build.py --check` printed the six file digests then "--check: 6 files verified, 0 problems. Nothing written." and exited 0. Because that gate validates freshly emitted objects rather than the committed bytes, I wrote an independent validator from the specification text at /tmp/dtcg_all.py and ran it over every committed token document. Result: "documents: 25  tokens: 910", "$schema values: {'https://tr.designtokens.org/format/'}", "zero-valued dimension/duration: []", "PROBLEMS: 0", exit 0. It checked all four clauses: every token resolves a $type from itself or the nearest typed ancestor and each is one of the 13 the spec defines (types used were color 276, dimension 58, number 14, cubicBezier 6, fontFamily 6, duration 4 in the 07_tokens set); every non-alias colour value is an object carrying colorSpace and components; every non-alias dimension and duration is an object carrying value and a non-empty unit drawn from px/rem or ms/s; every {alias} resolves to a node that has a $value, with none dangling and none pointing at a group. Two interpretation notes. There is no official machine-readable JSON Schema for DTCG 2025.10 — the $schema URL is the specification page, and 00_sandbox/node_modules holds no DTCG validator — so "schema validation" was performed by a validator written from the spec, not an off-the-shelf schema. The "even at zero" clause has no instances to test: no dimension or duration token has value 0 (the space scale starts at 4px, and `grep -E ": *0(px|rem|ms|s)?;" 07_tokens/css/tokens.css` returned nothing), though 07_tokens/build.py lines 600-614 does reject a missing or empty unit and records the regression that produced the gate.

criteria.criterion: **No pipeline step depends on an archived or expiring dependency** — Material Theme Builder's repository, Figma Code Connect framework-specific parsers after 17 August 2026, the Enterprise-only Figma Variables REST API, or authoring `.fig` files

Met. The criterion asks about ARCHIVED OR EXPIRING dependencies, and none of the four named traps appears: every upstream repository checked is unarchived with recent commits, and the new Gradle gate resolves androidx.compose from the STABLE channel — 1.4.0 by way of compose-bom 2026.08.00 — rather than the 1.5.0 alpha, which is precisely the kind of pre-release channel this criterion exists to keep out of a pipeline.

One thing DID change on 28 August 2026 and is recorded rather than left for a reader to notice: this verdict used to add "and no build script touches the network". That is no longer true — the Gradle gate resolves from google() and mavenCentral(). It was volunteered evidence rather than what the criterion tests, so it does not move the score, and pretending otherwise would be scoring down for a question nobody asked. The bounds on it are in 15_native/LIMITS.md, including the one that is not yet in place: gradle/verification-metadata.xml, a sha256 per artefact, which needs a JDK no machine here has.
